what: New: categorical exposures that switch back and forth
title: Inverse probability weighting with ipw
text: type = "", every interval contributes probability category observed , exposure can move categories directions. now works multinomial ordinal exposures. models pooled time, past exposure belongs formulas; previous dose level dose.lag.
code: set.seed(3) n.id <- 300 long <- data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(n.id), each = 4), time = rep(1:4, times = n.id)) long$l <- rnorm(nrow(long)) long$dose <- NA long$dose.lag <- NA for (t in 1:4) {   rows <- long$time == t   prev <- if (t == 1) rep(1, n.id) else long$dose[long$time == t - 1]   eta <- -1 + 0.8 * long$l[rows] + 0.7 * (prev - 1)   u <- runif(n.id)   long$dose.lag[rows] <- prev   long$dose[rows] <- ifelse(u < plogis(eta - 1.5), 3, ifelse(u < plogis(eta), 2, 1)) } long$dose <- factor(long$dose, levels = 1:3, labels = c("low", "medium", "high"),                     ordered = TRUE)  w.dose <- ipwtm(exposure = dose, family = "ordinal", link = "logit",                 numerator = ~ dose.lag, denominator = ~ dose.lag + l,                 id = id, timevar = time, type = "all", data = long) summary(w.dose$ipw.weights) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>  0.1015  0.6728  0.8916  1.0009  1.1278  6.3704 ipwplot(weights = w.dose$ipw.weights, timevar = long$time, binwidth = 1,         main = "Cumulative stabilized weights by visit")

title: ipw 1.3.1
text: CRAN release: 2026-10-30 Improved defensive input validation, parameter checking, error messages across core functions. Modernized formula construction (.formula()) eliminate fragile eval(parse(text = ...)) string manipulations. Fixed variable symbol evaluation issues passing variables function arguments rather raw names. Modularized ipwtm dedicated family modeling engines (binomial, survival, multinomial, ordinal, gaussian). Replaced manual survival hazard step-differencing continuous baseline hazard interpolation using survival::basehaz stats::approx. Refactored tstartfun use safe column evaluation direct vector lag logic (c(-1, t[-length(t)])). Upgraded testthat suite 3rd edition specs, expanding coverage multinomial, ordinal, gaussian, unstabilized models, weight truncation, invalid parameter rejection.
